observation: The architecture checked the plan against the code and found two things the plan would have shipped broken, and the plan said nothing about either. (1) Every subscription session was told 'Speak only if the subscription's instruction above asks you to' (provisioner.ts:1579), so nine empty prompts would have silenced the assistant for good. (2) A person's DM to the assistant woke it twice, once as a thread turn and once from the thread.message subscription, so every message would get two sessions and two answers. It also woke on its own creation. Both fixes became decisions (D-cetkyt, D-cd6tvw) and were proven: a DM records exactly one intent, and the no-instruction case passed 8/8 on all four harnesses.
evidence: architecture.md 0.1, 0.2, 4.2, 6.1; subscription-wake-once.integration.test.ts; review-1-harness.log 8 passed

observation: Section 0.4 decided without asking that a plugin lives in one scope at a time: a second team's install moves it, with no schema change. The plan only said that agents 'land on the team installed for'. Critique 1 blocked on this, because one-click Install from Settings makes silent eviction of the first team's agents a live path on a shared backend. The founder ruled per-team installs (D-c2gwsp). That added section 11, a migrations task, migration 0092 and a unique index. The plan had not covered two teams wanting the same plugin, and the architecture filled that gap itself instead of asking, even though it did flag its installScope interpretation.
evidence: critique-1.md blocker 1; architecture.md 0.4, 10 D-scope, 11; D-c2gwsp, D-9krr9a

Review 1's probe confirmed two distinct defaults rows, and the regression test from the install-folder fix was shown red by pointing defaultId back at the manifest name.
